The condition \( n^k \equiv 0 \pmod{k^n} \) translates to the requirement that for each prime \( q_j \) in the factorization of \( k \), the exponent of \( q_j \) in \( n^k \) must be at least \( n \times b_j \).

However, the problem does not provide specific values for \( n \) or any constraints on \( k \).
